# find all approximate copies: look for "GGCTTT" within 30bp upstream of a CTAAG

# Report on `region.fasta` (locus_006)

## Summary of the sequence
- **Length:** 3,000 bp; **GC content:** 49.1% (A 756, C 709, G 764, T 771) — unremarkable.
- **Coding potential:** None. The longest ORF on either strand is only **89 codons** (≈ positions 1634–1900). There are no long open reading frames, no recognizable start/stop-rich gene structure. The region behaves like non-coding DNA.

## Notable feature: a short repeated motif reiterated 8 times
The one thing that clearly stands out is an over-represented ~19-bp sequence, **`GGCTTTGGTTACTAAGGG`**, which occurs **8 times**, all in the **same (forward) orientation**, clustered in the 3′ third of the region.

| # | Start (1‑bp) | Copy (19 bp) | Mismatches vs consensus |
|---|--------------|--------------|--------------------------|
| 1 | 1963 | GGCTTTGG**TTACTAAGGG** | 0 |
| 2 | 2040 | GGCTT**T**T**G**TTACTAAGGG | 1 |
| 3 | 2114 | GGCTTTGGTTACTAAGGG | 0 |
| 4 | 2183 | GGCTTTG**T**T**T**TCTAAGGG | 2 |
| 5 | 2257 | GGCTTTGGTTACTAAGG**C** | 1 |
| 6 | 2315 | GGCTTTGGT**G**ACTAAGGG | 1 |
| 7 | 2389 | GGCTTTGGTTACTAAG**C**G | 1 |
| 8 | 2470 | GG**G**TTTGGTTACTAAGGG | 1 |

**Consensus:** `GGCTTTGGTTACTAAGGG` (an exact 20–21 bp version, `GACGGCTTTGGTTACTAAGGG`, occurs twice at 1960 and 2111).

**Array coordinates:** the eight copies lie within **positions 1963–2488** (≈526 bp), with individual copies at **1963–1981, 2040–2058, 2114–2132, 2183–2201, 2257–2275, 2315–2333, 2389–2407, 2470–2488**. There are **no copies anywhere else** in the 3,000 bp (upstream 1–1962 or downstream 2489–3000).

**Arrangement:** direct repeats with inter-copy spacings of 77, 74, 69, 74, 58, 74, 81 bp (mean ≈72 bp). No copy of the reverse complement exists, so there is no inverted-repeat/hairpin structure.

**Nature of the repeats:** only the ~19-bp motif itself is conserved — the sequences *between* copies are unrelated to one another. So this is **not** a smoothly diverged satellite/tandem array (no larger conserved repeat unit), and it is **not** a simple microsatellite (no tandem units of period 1–6 anywhere in the file). It looks more like a short motif that has been reiterated/dispersed eight times, or a "beaded" array where only the motif is under selection.

## Things that do *not* stand out
- No restriction sites of note, no poly-purine/poly-pyrimidine runs, no G-quadruplex tracts.
- Isolated single hits such as a `TATAAA` at 1465 and an `AATAAA` at 2819, and one `ACTAAG` at position 66, are consistent with random occurrence and are not part of any repeated structure.

## Bottom line
`locus_006` is a non-coding, ~49% GC, 3,000-bp region whose only striking property is a **reiterated ~19-bp motif (`GGCTTTGGTTACTAAGGG`), present in 8 direct copies between positions 1963 and 2488**, spaced on average ~72 bp apart and conserved only over the motif itself. Everything outside that ~530-bp window looks like ordinary low-feature genomic sequence.
